intended_object: The canonical equivalence between the category of costructured arrows from the diagonal functor T ⥤ T × T to (X₁, X₂), i.e. cones (Z, Z → X₁, Z → X₂), and the category of costructured arrows from Over.forget X₂ to X₁, i.e. objects Z → X₂ over X₂ together with a map Z → X₁. This is inferred from the docstring, which calls it the version of `ofDiagEquivalence` with the two projections swapped.
explanation:
The definition is a chain of three equivalences, and the types line up.

1. `ofDiagEquivalence X` gives `CostructuredArrow diag X ≌ CostructuredArrow (Over.forget X.1) X.2`.
2. `Over X.1` is by definition `CostructuredArrow (𝟭 T) X.1`, so `Over.forget X.1` is `CostructuredArrow.proj (𝟭 T) X.1`. Hence `ofCostructuredArrowProjEquivalence (𝟭 T) X.1 X.2` gives `≌ CostructuredArrow (Over.forget X.2 ⋙ 𝟭 T) X.1`.
3. `mapNatIso` with the right unitor removes the `⋙ 𝟭 T`.

The result sends an object (Z, f : Z → X.1, g : Z → X.2) to the object (Z, g) of `Over X.2` together with the map f to X.1. That is exactly the swapped version of `ofDiagEquivalence` that the docstring describes.

It is stated for an arbitrary category T, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has the unswapped version `ofDiagEquivalence` and the structured-arrow analogue `StructuredArrow.ofDiagEquivalence'`, but not this exact equivalence elsewhere; so `ofDiagEquivalence` is cited as the closest counterpart, not as a duplicate. Marking it `noncomputable` does not change what it defines.
